notes.title: For the Glory 1.3 is released!
notes.content:
Exactly 15 years after For the Glory 1.0 comes the FTG 1.3 update! Players who had switched to the 1.3 beta channel are encouraged to switch back to the main update channel to receive the update.

This is a [b]major content update[/b] with multiple new systems, new scenarios, an expanded timeline, user interface improvements, and new map modes.

For those already on the beta channel, this is mainly a bugfix and stabilization update. For those who hadn't tried the beta patches, here are some of the major changes you'll find since 1.2 (which itself is over 14 years old).

[h3][b]Major changes in FTG 1.3[/b][/h3]

- Fixed around two dozen separate crashes, some of them dating as far back as EU2
- Fixed several multiplayer out-of-sync issues
- Added new mapmodes:
  [list]
[*] Cultures
[*] Revolt risk
[*] Fortress levels
[*] Population
[*] Manpower
[*] Building locations
[*] Geographic (areas, regions, and continents)
[*] and several modding modes available only from the console
[/list]
- Revamped rebels:
[list]
[*] Different factions have different goals. You'll see Dutch rebels fighting under the tricolor before officially declaring independence, and you won't see rebels wandering across national borders without a good reason. Nationalist rebels may want to defect to their original country while peasants only want to overthrow the government.
[*] Hover over the revolt risk indicator in the province info screen to see which rebels are most likely to appear.
[*] If rebels capture a province, hover over the rebel shield in the province info screen to see what they are likely to do (declare independence, defect, or overthrow the government) and when they will be able do it.
[/list]
- New Holy Roman Empire screen shows the current emperor's support level and who is likely to be elected as the next emperor
  - A new notifier warning icon indicates if you are the current emperor but wouldn't remain emperor if a new election were called
- New peace offer mapmode allows you to offer or demand provinces by clicking them on the mapmode
- New building confirmation screen shows the estimated local and national effects of the building
- Missionary and colonist screens have new mouseover text showing a breakdown of the cost and chance
- New mouseover in sea zones explains straits and naval chokepoints
- Newly recruited armies and navies can now be automatically sent to a rally point
- New "Decisions" screen replaces old Missions screen
  - Potential decisions are shown in a list. Mouse over a decision to see the requirements.
  - All formable countries are now formed through decisions rather than events - now you can see exactly what it takes to form France as Navarre without having to read a script file.
- Many new formable countries, ranging from Lotharingia to Romania to the Il-Khanate to the Maurya Empire
- All AI interactions now indicate whether or not they are likely to succeed
- Maximum game resolution is now 2560x1440 (2k)
- Added four new scenarios: 1399, 1453, 1546, and 1816. Extended the game timeline to 1836 to reach Victoria.
- Rebalanced all existing scenarios and corrected many old errors in setup
- Added two new fantasy scenarios which use the same principle of colonizing a mostly empty map, but bring unique features:
[list]
[*] Fantasia Expanded has 24 playable factions set up against eight "boss" factions that will be far more advanced by the time players encounter them.
[*] Fantasia Imperium has 9 playable historical empire factions, 35 minor pagan factions to delay expansion, and a super-boss Atlantis with advanced technology and extremely aggressive AI.
[/list]
- Reduced randomization of combat - die rolls now favor middle numbers rather than being evenly distributed from 0 to 9.
- Eliminated many old exploits and minor annoyances
- Many small balance changes
- Hundreds of new historical leaders, monarchs, historical events, and random events
- Hundreds of new pictures for historical events
- Improved all areas of AI, especially money management, building investments, diplomacy, and military strategy
- Added many new modding triggers, commands, and other features (documented separately)
- Updated AGCEEP to version 1.60 which takes advantage of new 1.3 modding features (see the AGCEEP forum or PatchInfo160.txt in the AGCEEP mod folder for details)

See Changelog 1.3.txt in the FTG installation for full details.

notes.title: For the Glory 1.3 beta patches are now on Steam
notes.content:
Hello, Steam players!

We at Crystal Empire Games have not been idle since the last official patch 1.2 was released. In fact, we've built and released over a dozen beta patches on the Paradox forums in the last dozen years. But until now, the only way to acquire a beta patch was to download a zipped file from our website and extract it manually.

But as of today, 1.3 beta patches will be available in a Steam beta channel!

[b]To receive the current beta patch:[/b] Open your steam library, find "For the Glory: A Europa Universalis Game" in the list of your games, then right click on it and select "Properties".
In the Properties, select the "Beta" tab and select "1.3_beta_sep_2024" in the dropdown.

For those of you who didn't know about the forum patch releases, here's a PARTIAL list of highlights since 1.2:

[list]
[*]Fixed many, many crashes and multiplayer out-of-sync issues
[*]Added around 10 new mapmodes
[*]Completely revamped rebels with new factions and differing goals
[*]Many brand-new UI interactions, including new notifiers and an all-new Holy Roman Empire interface
[*]Improved AI
[*]A huge number of new modding/scripting features
[*]Increased maximum playable resolution from 1920x1080 to 2560x1440 (2k)
[*]Extended timeline from 1419-1819 to 1399-1837
[*]Four brand-new historical scenarios (1399, 1453, 1546, and 1816), two of which take advantage of the extended timeline
[*]Two new fantasy scenarios - build your empire through colonization and warfare, but watch out for the invasion of Atlantis!
[*]Complete overhaul of all existing scenarios for improved balance and historical accuracy
[*]Dozens of new countries to play, form, or revolt
[*]Formable countries can now be formed by player-driven decisions - you can see exactly what you need to form Russia rather than having to look up an event
[*]Hundreds of new historical events, leaders, and monarchs
[*]Hundreds of new pictures for historical events
[*]New map colorscale options (see the Settings screen in game)
[*]Reduced randomization of combat
[*]Updated the bundled AGCEEP mod to 1.60, including many updates that take advantage of new 1.3 modding features
[/list]

This is not even all of the highlights, let alone the minor bugfixes and polishing - you'll have to play the game to see what else is new!

(and... stay tuned, you might see the final 1.3 patch coming on a special day!)
